subject: test-planner
reason: One e2e case per reproduction URL: five sad cases for the non-numeric/empty brand and type links (including mixed numeric+text values that must still filter) and two happy regression cases for purely numeric brand and type links.

excluded.reason: out of scope; the story's Implementation Notes defer it as a follow-up
the Catalog API is unchanged; the defect is only in the WebApp page's query binding, which only e2e exercises
not among the ticket's steps; recorded under Open questions

excluded.item: Numeric ids that match no brand or type, negative or out-of-range numbers
excluded.reason: undefined by the story; recorded under Open questions

items.title: `/?brand=abc` shows the whole catalog with brand "All" selected
covers: Steps to Reproduce 1
Expected: steps 1-5 open the catalog page (HTTP 200, header, filters, product list)
Expected: steps 1, 2 and 5 show "101 products" with "All" selected
items.reason: Step 1 of the bug is the plainest form of the defect: a single non-numeric `brand` value made the page answer HTTP 500 with an empty body. The fix lives in the WebApp page's query binding, which only the rendered page on the test stack exercises, so this is e2e.

items.title: `/?type=abc` shows the whole catalog with type "All" selected
covers: Steps to Reproduce 2
Expected: steps 1-5 open the catalog page (HTTP 200, header, filters, product list)
Expected: steps 1, 2 and 5 show "101 products" with "All" selected
items.reason: Step 2 of the bug: `type` is bound separately from `brand`, so a fix to one could miss the other. A separate case proves the `type` parameter is guarded too. e2e because only the rendered WebApp page binds the query.

items.title: `/?brand=1&brand=abc` ignores "abc" and shows Daybird's 10 products
covers: Steps to Reproduce 3
Expected: a value that is not a number is ignored, and the other values still apply
Expected: step 3 shows Daybird's products, Daybird selected, "10 products", the same as step 6
items.reason: The ticket requires more than "no crash": the remaining numeric values must still filter. A fix that dropped the whole `brand` parameter on any bad value would pass TC-01 but fail here (it would show 101 products). e2e because the multi-value query binding only runs in the rendered page.

items.title: `/?type=7&type=x` ignores "x" and shows the 11 Navigation products
covers: Steps to Reproduce 4
Expected: a value that is not a number is ignored, and the other values still apply
Expected: step 4 shows the Navigation products, Navigation selected, "11 products", the same as /?type=7
items.reason: Same rule as TC-03 for the `type` parameter, which is bound on its own: a numeric type must still filter when a non-numeric one sits beside it. e2e for the same reason as the other cases.

items.title: `/?brand=` (empty value) shows the whole catalog with brand "All" selected
covers: Steps to Reproduce 5
Bug Report: an empty value
Expected: steps 1-5 open the catalog page (HTTP 200, header, filters, product list)
Expected: steps 1, 2 and 5 show "101 products" with "All" selected
items.reason: The empty value is the edge of "not a number" that the ticket names explicitly (a truncated link); it is parsed differently from text (an empty string, not a word), so it gets its own case. e2e because only the rendered page binds the query.

items.title: `/?brand=1` still shows Daybird's 10 products
covers: Steps to Reproduce 6
Expected: links with only numeric values work exactly as today
Actual: step 6 shows "10 products"
items.reason: The fix changes how `brand` is bound (strings parsed to ids); this guards that a purely numeric brand link still filters exactly as before. It is also the reference TC-03 is compared against. e2e on the rendered page.

items.title: `/?type=7` still shows the 11 Navigation products
covers: Expected: step 4 "the same as /?type=7"
Expected: links with only numeric values work exactly as today
items.reason: The `type` binding changed the same way as `brand`; this guards that a purely numeric type link still filters as before and is the reference TC-04 is compared against. e2e on the rendered page.

items.reason: Add an anonymous e2e case for /?type= asserting HTTP 200, the catalog header, filters, visible product cards, exactly "101 products", and type "All" selected. The story explicitly includes empty brand or type values; absence from the numbered reproduction steps does not make this undefined.

Extend both existing cases to assert that product cards are visible. Their current assertions allow an empty product list alongside a correct count and selected filter, although Expected explicitly requires the product list for every link in steps 1–5.

Expected says steps 1–5 show the product list, but TC-03 and TC-04 assert only the count text, not that product cards render. Add '.catalog-product count is greater than 0' to both, as TC-01, 02 and 05 do.
